questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses and the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy. You had to be very outreaching yourself sometimes to get the information needed. There were some information but it could have been more.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I started with a language course which I highly recommend. There you get a lot of information and you get used to beeing at campus as well as meeting a lot of new friends. 

The orientation days at Freie was the bare minimum. There were not really social arrangements and you had to fix everything your self. Also in regards to courses and selection the information was little.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found it through the Danish church. I can reccomend it. Otherwise, it seems easy to find housing. Try
wggesucht.de
or Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice. It seemed pretty crowded to live in a campus dorm and some were also far away from the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a mail from Freie Universität where they explain how you do. It is a bit "old" technologically and seems a bit outdated. I remember that there were many steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the incoming students mail to get help. Otherwise I talked with other peers who also went on exchange.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
The registration process for classes is a bit complicated. You can register for classes through Campus Management but also just ask the professer. Thus, there is two "systems" for registration. 

I got all the courses I wanted so in that way it was a good experience.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can recommend coming to a lot of different classes the first week and then register or deregister.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses were overall at a lower level academically than in my home university. However, I took some courses in German and they were very interesting. 
There is a lot of different courses to choose from. Sometimes, you can just write to the professor to ask if you can take the course if it's not a course on the institute.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level than home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Lot of class discussion. Not lectures. This is both positive, but I felt that sometimes people had not read the texts and then it felt a bit stupid to start discussing the text without a common understanding of the core arguments. 

Also it depends very much on the teacher how the style of teaching is. Some teachers were very good at structuring a discussion while some were more relaxed and didn't moderate the discussion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
15451	Resilienz demokratischer Systeme (Resilience of democratic Systems)

32520a	Lecture Series: US Foreign Policy in Turbulent Times

15461	Moderner Rechtsextremismus (Modern right-wing extremism)

15493	Deutsche Außenpolitik seit 1945
(German foreign policy since 1945)

31501a	Civil Society and Mobilization

15532	Knowledge politics and economy of conflict and violence part 1 & 2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend Democratic Resilience, German Foreign Policy, U.S. Foreign Policy, and Civil Society and Mobilization.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a semester fee at the university that covers transportation. Its the Deutschlands Ticket that gives you free transportation in Berlin and in all of Germany in all S-Bahn, Busses, U-Bahn and regional trains.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is not as expensive as in Denmark and going out for a drink at a bar. You have to remember to give tips.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join a club or sports programme.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of museums are available and free if you have the student card.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Museums, going to the lakes and Grunewald.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Leipzig, Dresden, Sächsische Schweiz.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take the language course. There is also a social and cultural programme to this.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything particular difficult or challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The vibe and kiez's in Berlin

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of bureaucracy at Freie, but it is still nice. 

Go in spring - Berlin is best in spring and summer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I became better at German.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: German courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
